articles.title: Who are the candidates short-listed for SC associate justice?
articles.summary: Marcos will pick his next SC associate justice appointee in place of retiring Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier

blocks.text: HIGHEST COURT. File photo of the Supreme Court of the Philippines.
Marcos will pick his next SC associate justice appointee in place of retiring Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier

items: The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has shortlisted 11 candidates for the position of Supreme Court associate justice, in place of retiring Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier.
Public interviews for the candidates were conducted on October 13 and 15, with the shortlist transmitted to Malacañang for presidential appointment.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – A total of 11 candidates have been short-listed by the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) for the position of Supreme Court (SC) associate justice vice Associate Justice Amy Lazaro Javier, who will retire on November 16.
Here are the short-listed candidates in alphabetical order:

items: Court of Appeals (CA) Associate Justice Ramon M. Bato Jr.
Solicitor General Darlene Marie B. Berberabe
Commission on Audit Chairperson Gamaliel A. Cordoba
CA Associate Justice Ramon A. Cruz
CA Associate Justice Maria Elisa Sempio Diy
CA Associate Justice Myra V. Garcia-Fernandez
CA Presiding Justice Fernanda Lampas Peralta
Commission on Elections Commissioner Ernesto P. Maceda, Jr.
CA Associate Justice Ronaldo Roberto B. Martin
CA Associate Justice Walter S. Ong
Court of Tax Appeals Associate Justice Maria Rowena M. San Pedro

blocks.text: Under the 1987 Constitution, the JBC is mandated to screen applicants for the judiciary and the Office of the Ombudsman. After the screening, the JBC will conduct public interviews of the qualified candidates. A deliberation will follow, then the council will submit a short list to the president who will then make the appointment.

In this case, the JBC held the public interviews for the new candidates on October 13 and 15. It no longer interviewed bets who already went through the process since their interviews were still valid.

The judiciary is independent, but it is the president who is constitutionally mandated to make appointments to the courts. In this case, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. will appoint his next justice to the High Court after Lazaro Javier reaches the mandatory age of 70 next month.
According to the SC, the short list has already been transmitted to Malacañang.

An SC justice must be a natural-born citizen, at least 40 years old, and have been a judge or law practitioner in the Philippines for at least 15 years or more. This is found under Section 7(1), Article VIII of the 1987 Constitution.

blocks.caption: Part 1: New candidates in the running to be Marcos’ 2nd SC justice
Part 2: Old-timer bets in the running to be Marcos’ 2nd SC justice

blocks.text: On top of this, a JBC 2020 rule states that an SC justice must serve a minimum of 2.5 years. This means that the eldest age of a candidate should be 67.5 years old, since the mandatory retirement age for justices is 70 years old.
On Thursday, the JBC also published the short list of chief justice nominees. These are the five candidates seeking to succeed Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo:

items: Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen
Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa
Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda
Associate Justice Japar Dimaampao
Associate Justice Jose Midas Marquez

blocks.text: The chief justice and associate justice posts will be Marcos’ second and third appointee to the SC, which is currently dominated by appointees of former president Rodrigo Duterte. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Marcos attends Michelin Guide 2027 ceremony
articles.summary: Marcos is the first sitting head of state in history to attend a Michelin Guide restaurant unveiling.

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 5:30pm
MANILA, Philippines (Updated 6:10 p.m.) — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. attended the Michelin Guide Manila & Cebu 2027 ceremony on Thursday, October 29, at the Manila Marriott Hotel in Pasay City.
First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos also attended the ceremony, where Marcos became the first sitting head of state in history to attend a Michelin Guide restaurant unveiling.
The chief executive’s presence at the red-carpet event underscores the Philippine government’s strategic push to position the country as a premier global culinary destination.

Addressing an audience of acclaimed chefs, restaurateurs and media representatives, Marcos emphasized the vital role of Filipino hospitality and culinary heritage in driving economic growth and cultural diplomacy.
"The Philippines joined that journey only last year, but Filipino cuisine is already finding its place at the table," Marcos said.
The guide's inaugural Philippine edition recognized 108 establishments, including 25 Bib Gourmand selections and nine Michelin-starred restaurants.
"For Filipinos, food is never just about food. It is how we welcome guests, how we bring our families together, and share a little of ourselves with others," he said.
Marcos cited traditional dishes such as adobo, kinilaw and sisig as examples of how Filipino cuisine reflects the country's resourcefulness and the richness of ingredients found across its islands.

He also highlighted local establishments recognized by the guide, including Morning Sun Eatery in Quezon City, known for its traditional Ilocano dishes, and Casa Palma, whose chef, Aaron Isip, honed his craft in Paris before returning to the Philippines. The restaurant has since earned one Michelin star.

"Our country is known for our beautiful islands, our rich history, and our vibrant culture. Now, our cuisine can become another reason for travelers to visit, explore our regions, and to stay longer," Marcos said.
He also noted that nine Philippine hotels and resorts received Michelin Keys in 2026, including the country's first two properties to earn two keys.

Marcos said the growing interest in Filipino cuisine could benefit local producers and communities, citing Gallery by Chele, where chef Chele González showcases indigenous rice varieties from the Cordilleras.
"Greater interest in Filipino cuisine can mean more opportunities for our farmers, our fisherfolk, food producers, and our MSMEs," Marcos said.

"For our part, government will continue to improve infrastructure, and air and sea connectivity to make these destinations more accessible. We also support culinary education and skills development for aspiring chefs and hospitality professionals," he added.
The ceremony was held in conjunction with the Department of Tourism, led by Tourism Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay, and coincided with the global centennial celebration of the Michelin Guide.
The 2027 edition marks the guide's second annual selection in the country, expanding its footprint across Manila, its environs and Cebu.

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 5:22pm
A prosecution witness on Thursday said that he saw Senator Jinggoy Estrada when he delivered 12 boxes to him.

Vergel Nino Garcia, former aide of state witness and ex-Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) undersecretary Roberto Bernardo, made the testimony during the hearing on the bail petition filed by suspended Senator Estrada amid a P573-million plunder case against him.
The case involves Estrada’s alleged receipt of kickbacks.
Garcia said that upon his delivery of 12 boxes for Estrada at the Artiaga Building in San Juan City in November 2024, he spotted Estrada in the same area wearing a t-shirt, pants and leather shoes.
Garcia said he did not see what was inside the boxes which he delivered upon the instructions of Bernardo.
After the delivery, Garcia said he called Bernardo to inform him that the delivery was made.
During the said delivery, Garcia also said he was accompanied by Bernardo’s driver, Francisco dela Fuente.

Aside from Estrada, Garcia said he also delivered boxes to former senator Bong Revilla, former Public Works secretary Manuel Bonoan (15 boxes), the late former DPWH Undersecretary Maria Catalina Cabral (one box and one paper bag) and former Education undersecretary Trygve Olaivar (eight suitcases and 15 boxes).
During the questioning by Estrada’s defense counsels, Garcia also said that they did not take photos or videos during the delivery.
A day earlier, Bernardo said there were four deliveries of commitments or kickbacks to Estrada from 2024 to 2025, but he was only present for one delivery in June 2025.
Bernardo later said it wasn’t easy for him to implicate Senator Jinggoy Estrada whom he accused of receiving kickbacks from government projects.
Bernardo made such position when asked as to why he did not implicate Estrada in his earlier affidavit.

“During that time [of my first affidavit], I have no confirmation, I have no solid evidence that will prove [his involvement]. I have already in [my] mind that he is a proponent [of projects], but I have to confirm [first],” Bernardo said.
“Ang hirap po ipahamak ang kaibigan. Hindi ko po kaagad magagawa iyon. Kailangan may solid evidence po," Bernardo added.
(It is tough to betray a friend. I cannot do that easily. I need to have solid evidence.)

Bernardo also pointed out that his previous affidavit, made prior to 2026, provides that given the complexities in the case, he reserved his right to “execute a supplemental affidavit if warranted.” — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
articles.summary: The jailbreak began with a fake seizure and ended 36 hours later with all the inmates back behind bars.

blocks.text: A fake medical emergency, an audacious jailbreak and a 36-hour search operation that ended with 17 prisoners being recaptured.
Those are the highlights of a story from India's Tamil Nadu state that has captured headlines across the country.
It began on Monday night after 17 men escaped from a prison in Theni district in the southern state after overpowering guards, and ended almost two days later with police catching them in batches.

The incident has drawn attention to overcrowding in Indian prisons. Police say the Theni prison was housing 334 inmates against a capacity of 200, leaving authorities unable to maintain control once chaos broke out.
The state police said it has suspended nine staff at the prison for alleged negligence in connection with the incident.
All the men who escaped were undertrials - inmates on trial or awaiting one - and 18 of them were in one cell at the prison in Thekkampatti in Theni.

On Monday night at 2230 local time (17:00 GMT), one of the prisoners acted like he was going through a seizure. The other cellmates shouted for help and a jail official responded. He was soon overpowered by the prisoners, police said.

The prisoners then got out of the cell, reportedly attacked two other jail guards and took away keys which they used to open the main gate and flee. While 17 escaped, one returned to the prison immediately.
Several prison personnel were injured in the attack.

items: The 'mastermind' behind India's biggest jailbreak

blocks.text: Police sources told BBC Tamil that they were examining the possibility of collusion between some prison officials and the escaped men.
Sandeep Rathore, Director General of Police for Prisons in Tamil Nadu, said in a press briefing that the jailbreak was caused by "human error".
"There was a clear breach of security protocol as the prisoners managed to pass through a three-tier barrier manned by security personnel," he said.

At the time of the incident, only four guards were on duty, far below the staffing required to maintain the prescribed 1:6 guard-to-inmate ratio recommended by the state - which should have worked out to 34 guards against the approved strength of 200 prisoners.
The police then launched a manhunt, calling forces from across the state.
"Advanced technology, drone surveillance, CCTV footage analysis, and the tireless efforts of police personnel played a crucial role," the department said in a statement on X.
Four men were arrested at a bus station in a nearby village, and the fifth was caught while he was travelling in a tuk-tuk.

A drone search of a forest near the prison led to eight more escaped prisoners being caught. Videos of the arrests showed the men obeying police instructions even as they did not answer questions from reporters who were also seen at the scene.
Two more were captured with the help of drone surveillance, police said, while the last two men surrendered on Wednesday.
News agency PTI reported that all 17 recaptured prisoners have been moved to high-security correctional prisons.
Rathore told media that all prisons across the state would be audited to check if rules were being followed.

The incident evoked memories of one of the biggest jailbreaks in Tamil Nadu in 1995 when 43 suspected militants escaped from a special camp after digging a 153-foot-long tunnel beneath a historic fort. Some of them were never recaptured.

While the investigation is going on, the incident has sparked a conversation on overcrowding in Indian prisons. The National Crime Records Bureau's last Prison Statistics India report from 2023 showed a national occupancy rate of 120.1%.

Data shows that undertrial prisoners - individuals who are detained while they await police investigation or court trials - make up more than 73% of India's total prison population. Human rights groups and legal experts have also raised concerns about delays in investigations and trials that lead to people languishing for years behind bars.
Additional reporting by Siraj and Prabhurao Anandhan

articles.title: UNDAS 2026: NLEX expects passenger surge on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026
articles.summary: The North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) is expecting a surge in passengers starting Friday afternoon, October 30 as Filipinos go on exodus in observance of All Saints" Day and All Souls" Day this weekend.

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 5:14pm
The North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) is expecting a surge in passengers starting Friday afternoon, October 30 as Filipinos go on exodus in observance of All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day this weekend.

“Ito po ay ine-expect natin mga bukas ng hapon, early afternoon po siguro. Tuloy-tuloy po yan hanggang gabi. And then early morning po ng Saturday hanggang hapon na po siguro ng Saturday, 'Yun po 'yung ating pa-norte,” said NLEX Corporation AVP for Traffic Operations Robin Ignacio in an interview with Balitanghali.

(We are expecting this around tomorrow afternoon, probably early afternoon. That will continue until night. And then early morning on Saturday until probably Saturday afternoon—that's for our northbound traffic.)
The NLEX official said that traffic along the expressway is still fastmoving, especially going north.
But the toll operator said it’s not expecting a big difference between the volume of passengers in this year’s Undas compared to last year.

“Baka hindi naman po gano'n kaano po 'yung difference ano, pero pa from 'yung ating normal daily average, ine-expect po namin na maaari po itong tataas ng between 3 to 5% ito pong period ng today, October 29 hanggang November 3,” said Ignacio.
(The difference might not be that huge, but compared to our normal daily average, we expect that it could rise between 3% to 5% during this period from today, October 29, until November 3.)

“Pero siyempre, meron po tayong 'yung mga peak hours na sinasabi po namin kagaya nung nabanggit ko po kanina 'yung dagsa. Maaari pong 'yung hourly traffic po natin no'n kompara sa normal daily, normal hourly traffic natin eh baka magiging mas mahigit pa po ng 20% 'yung itataas nung peak hours na 'yon,” he added.

(But of course, we have what we call peak hours, just like the surge I mentioned earlier. Our hourly traffic then, compared to our normal daily or normal hourly traffic, might increase by more than 20% during those peak hours.)
Further, NLEX said that it has already deployed around 1,500 personnel starting today.
“Tinataya po namin nasa mga 1,500 personnel mula po sa mga toll tellers po natin, mga patrol, security, traffic marshal at saka 'yung ating incident response teams,” said Ignacio.
(We estimate around 1,500 personnel, ranging from our toll tellers, patrols, security, traffic marshals, to our incident response teams.) — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: China blames ‘self-serving’ PH politician for scaled-back ASEAN defense presence
articles.summary: China said on Thursday, October 29, it sent only its Manila-based defense attaché to a top regional defense meeting in Cebu because a “self-serving” Philippine politician had…

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 5:12pm
Senior Captain Yang Lei, the defense attache of the Chinese Embassyin Manila, attends the ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting-Plus in Cebu, Oct. 29, 2026.
Screengrab via ASEAN livestream

MANILA, Philippines — China said on Thursday, October 29, it sent only its Manila-based defense attaché to a top regional defense meeting in Cebu because a “self-serving” Philippine politician had abused the country’s chairship to block its participation.

Stressing that the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) operates on ASEAN’s principle of “consensus through consultation,” the Chinese defense ministry said Manila’s moves violated that rule and undermined Beijing’s “legitimate rights” as a member of the mechanism.

“As the rotating chair of this year’s ADMM-Plus, the Philippine side has allowed a certain self-serving politician to act recklessly and abuse its chairmanship to put up obstacles to China’s participation,” ministry spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang told a press conference in Beijing.
Zhang did not name the politician or describe the obstacles.
He also said “many ASEAN countries have raised questions and opposition over this,” without identifying any of them.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., who chaired this year’s meetings, dismissed that account at a press conference as the two-day gathering in Cebu closed.
“So far as ASEAN is concerned, I do not believe our ASEAN member countries feel that way. If not, they would have let me know,” Teodoro said. “So it is China’s position, it is not ASEAN’s position.”

China, a dialogue partner rather than an ASEAN member, could be accommodated only “subject to rules and limitations,” he said, and was given the chance to state a position “not any different from what they have been articulating before.”
“No country has the right to characterize ASEAN processes except ASEAN member countries,” Teodoro added.
China’s envoy this year — a naval officer already in Manila as the defense attaché of the Chinese Embassy — was its lowest-level representation at the ADMM-Plus since the forum began in 2010.
Teodoro personally welcomed arriving heads of delegation at the Mactan Expo Center in Lapu-Lapu City, including deputy defense ministers from dialogue partners who rank below him.
But it was Defense Undersecretary Ignacio Madriaga who received Senior Captain Yang Lei upon his arrival in Cebu, standing in for Teodoro Jr., a move seen as a tit-for-tat downgrade in protocol.
Historically, Beijing would send its defense minister to attend the summit, which is also the region’s largest annual gathering of defense chiefs.

The ADMM-Plus groups ASEAN’s 11 members with eight dialogue partners — Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia and the United States — and builds on the ADMM, ASEAN’s highest defense consultative body since 2006.
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles were among the defense chiefs who attended the meeting in Cebu.

In his remarks, Zhang described the ADMM-Plus as “the highest-level and largest defense and security dialogue and cooperation mechanism in the Asia-Pacific,” one that has served as “an important platform for countries to build trust, strengthen cooperation, and uphold regional peace and stability.”
The Philippine side’s moves, he said, “run counter to the open and inclusive spirit of the ADMM-Plus” and “do not conform to basic diplomatic protocols.”

articles.title: N.S. premier doubles down on complaint to professor over AI data centre comments
articles.summary: Premier Tim Houston says he's glad his communications adviser sent a critical email to a professor who commented on a proposed data centre. Houston claims Sibo Chen was "clearly lacking information…

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New

Premier Tim Houston says he's glad his communications adviser sent a critical email to a professor who commented on a proposed data centre. Houston claims Sibo Chen was "clearly lacking information but yet speaking as an expert." Chen suggested the email was meant to intimidate him.
Premier Tim Houston says he's glad his communication adviser sent the critical email
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Oct 29, 2026 5:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: 1 hour ago

A staffer from Premier Tim Houston's office emailed a complaint last week to a Toronto Metropolitan University professor and included a CBC News reporter and the chair of the professor's department on the email.
Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston is doubling down on a complaint his office sent to a university professor in Toronto who commented on a proposed artificial intelligence data centre.
A staffer from Houston's office sent the complaint last week, emailing a copy of the message to a CBC News reporter and the chair of the professor's department.
Speaking to reporters Wednesday, Premier Tim Houston said he's glad his communications adviser sent the critical email.
"I'm happy he sent that message to provide some additional information to somebody who was clearly lacking in information but yet speaking as an expert," Houston said.

The feedback came after Sibo Chen, an associate professor of communication at Toronto Metropolitan University, gave a media interview to CBC saying that public concerns about the data centre project over water usage and electricity rate hikes were valid.
William Burns, a communications adviser with the premier's office, said Chen's "slanted comments" were irresponsible and not backed by research on the local community.
Sibo Chen, an associate professor in the Toronto Metropolitan University's school of professional communication, is shown in this undated handout photo. (Sibo Chen/Handout/The Canadian Press)
"Nova Scotians deserve facts, not speculation presented in a way that creates unnecessary anxiety," said Burns' email, which Chen shared with The Canadian Press.

Members of the public and opposition parties in the province have expressed concerns about Everwind Fuels' proposed multi-billion dollar data centre, which would be leased to U.S. AI company Anthropic for 20 years.
A petition to stop the development of AI data centres in Nova Scotia on Change.org had over 24,000 signatures as of Wednesday afternoon.
'I'm becoming the subject of my own study,' Chen says
Chen suggested that copying the department chair implies the government was trying to intimidate him.
"I actually study how scholars get harassed when they go to do knowledge mobilization ... I'm becoming the subject of my own study," he said.
Chen says he has studied environmental controversies in Canada for 10 years and this is the first time he has received a complaint from a premier's office.
Comments 'should send a chill down peoples' spines, Chender says

"I'm very critical about the oilsands, but I never received a complaint from the premier's office in Alberta," he said in a video interview Wednesday. His comments, he said, were about the general implications of AI data centre development and backed by peer-reviewed research.
The premier said he doesn't know how often his team reaches out to academics to criticize the comments they make to the media.
"I'm not sure how often we are communicating with people who are presenting in the media, but I hope it's a lot," Houston said.

"If somebody is presenting themselves as an expert and speaking definitively on something that they're wrong on, I think it's incumbent on all of us … [to] say there's some information you're missing," he added.
Nova Scotia NDP Leader Claudia Chender called Houston's comments disturbing.

"The comments that we heard just now from the premier, that he hopes that his staff are reaching out to people in the media regularly to correct them on their professional point of view, that should actually send a chill down peoples' spines," Chender told reporters Wednesday.
Data centre criticism
Chender said the premier's comments lead her to believe that his staff are "bullying" independent experts who criticize his government's projects.

The 18,600-square-metre data centre would draw 95 megawatts of electricity in its first phase and 420 megawatts after an expected expansion in mid-2028. Everwind says it will cover the cost of all electricity infrastructure so that project will not increase power rates.
Everwind estimates that the facility will use an average of 100,000 litres of water per day in its first phase and 500,000 litres per day after the expansion is completed.

items: EverWind proposes binding agreement with N.S. on data centre rules
Houston says he's willing to sign agreement with data centre on water usage, power rates

blocks.text: In his email to Chen, Burns said the government will not support a project that increases power rates to customers.

He also highlighted another CBC interview, where Lois Landry, the warden of Richmond County explained there are provisions in place to protect residents and limit the amount of water the data centre would draw from nearby Lake Landrie.
Burns also suggested that as a professor from a Toronto university, Chen could not understand the impact of data centre in Nova Scotia.
EverWind's data centre will be in Point Tupper, just outside Port Hawkesbury, N.S. (Taryn Grant/CBC)
Chen said the response from Burns suggests the government is sending the message that citizens don't need to be concerned about the project.
However, he said the province hasn't provided enough information to the public about the proposed data centre and he understands why Nova Scotians are worried.
Chen said local university professors may not feel comfortable expressing their concerns about the data centre after seeing the pushback he received from the Nova Scotia government.
"I think that's precisely why people don't want to comment on this," he said.

articles.title: How genetic genealogy helped police find witnesses — but not the suspect — in the Byron Carr murder case
articles.summary: When Charlottetown police first announced a break in a high-profile cold case, they credited investigative genetic genealogy with helping identify a suspect. Newly released court documents shed more…

image.caption: Court documents made public after the charges against Todd Joseph Irving were dropped detail how investigative genetic genealogy led police to witnesses who would provide the evidence that led to an arrest in the decades-old murder case. (iStock)

blocks.text: WARNING: This story contains disturbing details.

When Charlottetown police first announced a break in a high-profile cold case, they credited investigative genetic genealogy with helping identify a suspect. Newly released court documents shed more light on how police set their sights on the man who was charged with first-degree murder before all charges in the case were dropped earlier this month.

Byron Carr was found dead in his home on Nov. 12, 1988. The 36-year-old teacher had been strangled with a towel and stabbed with a kitchen knife. Carr's wallet was missing, an extinguished cigarette butt had been placed in his navel, and the words "I will kill again" were written on the bedroom wall.

items: How did a P.E.I. cold case fall apart just before it was set to go to trial?

blocks.text: It wasn't until 2024 that Todd Joseph Irving was arrested and charged with first-degree murder and interfering with human remains. He pleaded not guilty before both charges were withdrawn by the Crown.

Court documents made public after the charges were dropped detail how investigative genetic genealogy led police not to their suspect, but to witnesses who more than 30 years later would provide the evidence that led them to make an arrest.
Carr was last seen in downtown Charlottetown in the early morning hours of Nov. 11, 1988. Earlier that night, he'd been out with friends at Pat's Rose and Grey Room, a Charlottetown bar at the time.
A neighbour told police she saw two men fleeing from Carr's backyard at about 9 p.m. on Nov. 11. His body was found the following morning.
According to an autopsy report, the cause of death was mechanical asphyxia and the knife found in Carr's abdomen was inserted after he was already dead.
Byron Carr was found dead in his home on Nov. 12, 1988. The 36-year-old teacher had been strangled with a towel and stabbed with a kitchen knife. (Family photo)

Police have long said they believed Carr was killed during what began as a consensual sexual encounter and that the killer initially fled but returned hours later with an accomplice to stage the scene: taking Carr's wallet, scrawling the message on the wall and stabbing him.
Three DNA profiles were eventually found at the scene:

items: Male 1, whose DNA was extracted from the cigarette butt found in Carr's navel, from swabs taken from the body, and from a pair of underwear found wrapped in the bedding underneath the body.
Female 1, whose DNA was also found on the underwear beneath Carr's body. That female has never been identified, according to the documents.

Male 2, whose DNA was found on a pair of socks that had been on top of the trash can in Carr's kitchen after they were sent for analysis in 2009. According to the documents, it was "common police knowledge" that socks were used by perpetrators at the time to prevent leaving fingerprints.

blocks.text: It wasn't until May of 2023 that — according to multiple documents submitted in 2026 as part of Irving's application to be released on bail, including an agreed statement of facts — police say the contributor of Male 2's profile was identified thanks to investigative genetic genealogy.

At the time of Irving's arrest, police said they'd also arrested a second suspect who had been interviewed and released without being charged. According to that same agreed statement of facts, that was the man whose DNA was found on the socks. CBC News is not naming him because he hasn't been charged with a crime.

items: After 35 years, DNA evidence leads to 1st-degree murder charge in P.E.I. cold case
Genetic genealogy was key to the Byron Carr homicide investigation. Here's how it works

blocks.text: There's no mention of a suspected accomplice in any of the many court documents reviewed by CBC News, and there's no indication police believe Male 2 was involved. According to a 2013 interview with CBC News, police said at that time they believed they had identified the person who returned to help stage the scene roughly 12 hours after the murder, but that person died years before he was identified. Police did not release his name.

But Male 2 did work at Pat's Rose and Grey Room at the time, and according to multiple documents including a pre-trial submission outlining the Crown's theory, police believed that Male 1 would be found in the group of people who either worked at or were connected to Pat's Rose and Grey Room.

That hunch led them to a witness who worked at the bar in the 1980s and said he remembered working with Todd Joseph Irving, who used to use the last name Gallant. That witness said he saw a news broadcast that showed the handwriting left on the wall of Carr's bedroom and noted that it was similar to Irving's.
"[That witness] described the accused as a 'strongly built and violent young man who bragged' about engaging in 'gay bashing' by picking up gay men and beating them up," reads the Crown's theory.

"Todd Gallant told [the witness] that he would meet gay men at night, go with them to a secluded area and then beat them up," reads a separate agreed statement of facts submitted as part of a 2025 court hearing.
The words 'I will kill again' were written on the wall of Byron Carr's bedroom. (Charlottetown Police Services)

According to the Crown's theory, that interview led police to obtain documents they say contained Irving's handwriting, and investigators concluded there were "striking similarities" between that document and the message left on the wall at the crime scene, "including the circle over the letter 'i,' and the letters 'a' and 'g.'"
Police learned that Irving had left P.E.I. in the years after Carr was killed, living in Texas and Arkansas before returning to the Island in 2022, according to the 2025 agreed statement of facts.
DNA had a 'high probability' of being a match to Male 1

Weeks after comparing the handwriting samples, the document goes on to say, investigators seized two bags of trash from the black bin placed at the end of Irving's driveway and sent several items — four cigarette butts and two coffee cups — for DNA analysis.

In October of 2023, according to the agreed statement of facts and DNA analysis documents reviewed by CBC News, those samples came back as a likely match for the DNA found on Carr's body, as well as the cigarette butt and underwear left at the scene.

"Through further investigation, police determined the accused's DNA had a high probability of being a match to the Male 1 profile," reads the Crown's theory. "In particular, the chances of an unrelated member of the Caucasian population sharing the same profile was determined to be 1 in 45 trillion."

According to several documents filed in 2026 as part of Irving's bail application, the man identified as Male 2 denied any involvement in Carr's death but when interviewed by police said he knew Irving and described him as "a strong 'goofy' kid at the time of the murder." According to a transcript of a police interview filed as part of the bail application, Irving's sister described the two men as friends.

Police have long said they believed Carr was killed in his Lapthorne Avenue home during what began as a consensual sexual encounter and that the killer initially fled but returned hours later with an accomplice to stage the scene. (CBC)
According to the Crown's theory, it's believed Male 2's socks were taken and used to avoid leaving fingerprints when the scene was staged, after Carr was already dead.

"It is anticipated that [Male 2] will testify that he took the Applicant [Irving] under his wing around the time of the victim's death," reads a submission from the Crown filed during the bail hearings. "The Applicant was, at that time, a man of very limited means who would borrow clothes and would regularly visit [Male 2]'s home."

According to an affidavit filed in May of 2026 as part of his bail application, Irving's defense argues the case against him was based on circumstantial evidence and no direct witnesses connected him with Carr's death.
The affidavit goes on to say that Irving's defence didn't dispute the DNA evidence in the case.

"I have been informed by my legal counsel and believe it to be true that DNA matching my genetic profile is located on the victim's body," the affidavit reads. "That does not mean I killed Mr. Carr or that I interfered with his body."
The man police accused of murdering Byron Carr in 1988 is now free. Here's what happened
The affidavit goes on to question the Crown's theory that Carr was killed during a consensual sexual encounter.
"My understanding is that the Crown's theory in relation is that Mr. Carr was killed during the sexual encounter. I do not believe this can necessarily be established," the affidavit reads.
"I would point out issues with the Crown's theory to show that my involvement in this matter is not certain or predetermined," the affidavit goes on to say.
The affidavit goes on to argue that over the years, four separate tips to police identified the handwriting as belonging to four other suspects.
"It is a triable issue as to who is the author of the handwriting on the wall as clearly members of the public view the handwriting as [possibly] written by other people."

items: Independent review ordered into Byron Carr murder investigation after charges dropped
How did a P.E.I. cold case fall apart just before it was set to go to trial?

blocks.text: Ultimately, none of the evidence will be tested at trial. Weeks before the case was set to go to trial, the Crown announced that all charges against Irving had been dropped because Charlottetown police lost substantial physical evidence connected to the case.
At a bail hearing in July, it was revealed that both the knife found at the scene and the towel used to strangle Carr were missing.
Police have said they knew as far back as 2007 that physical evidence was missing, but believed the DNA evidence would be enough.
The Crown said it didn't know about any missing evidence until that July bail hearing, and was no longer confident it could secure a conviction.

articles.title: Bato dela Rosa's world getting smaller as authorities step up manhunt ops --Palace
articles.summary: Malacañang on Thursday defended anew the P50 million bounty set on Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa"s head, saying that his world has gotten smaller as authorities have stepped up efforts to arrest…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 4:44pm

Malacañang on Thursday defended anew the P50 million bounty set on Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa’s head, saying that his world has gotten smaller as authorities have stepped up efforts to arrest him.

“Totoo na lumiliit ang mundo ni Senator Bato dahil ang maaaring makakita sa kaniya ay magbibigay ng impormasyon agad-agad sa PNP at sa ibang law enforcement agencies,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a press briefing.
(It is true that Senator Bato’s world is getting smaller because whoever sees him could give information immediately to the PNP and other law enforcement agencies.)
Reading a statement from the Department of Interior and Local Government (DILG) and the Philippine National Police (PNP), Castro said that the agencies have stepped up their manhunt for Dela Rosa.

“The combined effect of heightened police operations increase public awareness and the bounty announcement has substantially narrowed the senator's ability to move freely without drawing attention,” Castro said, reading the joint statement.
“We likewise appeal to Senator Dela Rosa to voluntarily surrender to the proper authorities and submit himself to the legal process with dignity,” she added.
However, she did not disclosure more details regarding the operations.
Castro said that all information being received is carefully reviewed and credible leads are being acted upon.
The task force, led by Police Lieutenant General Wilson Joseph Lopez, is currently ensuring seamless coordination among all concerned agencies, she added.
The Palace official also emphasized that the P50 million bounty for Dela Rosa came from the confidential funds of the DILG.

Dela Rosa’s camp has sought the intervention of the Supreme Court in the manhunt against him in relation arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court. He sought a temporary restraining order to prevent the government from arresting him. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
articles.summary: The recordings appear to show one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another up ahead had stalled.

blocks.text: Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 68 people and injured dozens.
Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.

Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.
The release of the recordings comes as Spain begins three days of national mourning for one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.
One train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train run by private operator Iryo, with 147 passengers.
A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.
But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.

Audio recordings published by Spanish news outlets including El Pais and RTVE reveal the conversations that took place between the two train's drivers and the control centre in the Spanish capital ahead of the crash.
In one recording, a control centre operator tells the Renfe driver to resume its journey at normal speed after some technical issues.
"Continue your journey and then proceed under [Lateral Signalling Block], at normal speed with normal operation," the control centre operator says to the driver.
The driver replies, "At normal speed?" To which the controller says: "Yes."
The Lateral Signaling Block is a back-up or alternative train system used when the automatic signalling or data transmission system fails.
Later, the driver of the other Iryo train says in another audio recording that communication with the train-control system has been lost and they are stationary at Urda.
The train "is stationary in front of the entry signal at Urda", the driver tells the control centre operator. After a series of exchanges, the driver is then told to "resume the journey" normally.

The Iryo driver then contacts the control centre again, according to a later recording, saying they cannot start the train. "The train won't allow me to control the [security] system. That's why I am still stopped in front of the entry signal," they say.
The latter recording suggests that the controller had been notified that the Iryo train remained stationary as the Renfe train approached.
Iryo said its train, which had 147 passengers on board, was "struck from behind" by another train, by Renfe train which was carrying 397 passengers.
Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente said on Wednesday that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was "inexplicable".
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the "whole of Spain is grieving", adding that "lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart, the pain is immense".
Emergency crews worked through the night under powerful floodlights to cut open metal carriages in the search for victims, with many of those killed in the crash still to be identified.

Hundreds of personnel have been deployed to the disaster site to assist with recovery efforts, according to Spain's interior ministry, with drones and helicopters being used to find victims and remove rubble.
Witnesses described seeing people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.

Sánchez said it was "unacceptable" that Spain had suffered two serious rail disasters this year, after a high-speed crash killed 46 people near Córdoba in January. It occurred on the same line as Wednesday's accident, but much further south.
Most political parties suspended campaigning for upcoming elections following the incident.

The exception was the far-right party Vox. Its leader, Santiago Abascal, said his party would not take part in what he described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure.

articles.title: Healey accused of a ‘complete failure’ to target energy bill support at those most in need – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Resolution Foundation says ‘poorest half of households will gain… just £14 more than the £144 received by the richest half’

Good morning. The day after the budget is often the moment when…

blocks.text: Good morning. The day after the budget is often the moment when big initiatives announced by the chancellor the day before with a flourish start to unravel as experts pore over the small print. There is not much of that happening this morning – mainly because John Healey did not have any really big initiatives up his sleeve. Compared with a normal budget, his tax and spending initiatives were mostly relatively minor. That means that the opposition parties have been struggling to find things to attack, and so instead they have resorted to criticising Healey for what he did not do: slash welfare (the Tory/Reform UK solution), or join the EU’s single market (the Lib Dems’).

Healey has given interviews to all the main broadcasters, which are playing out this morning, but they were recorded last night and they don’t have any sensational new revelations. As Rowena Mason reports, one of the top lines was Healey saying he would cut welfare spending before the election.
But there were other lines in the interviews too. I will be posting all the highlights this morning.

The two main public spending thinktanks, the Institute for Fiscal Studies and the Resolution Foundation, are both publishing reports assessing the budget this morning. The RF has issued a news release with its main findings and its assessment of the overall economic impact of the budget measures highlights three problems.

items: It accuses Healey of a “complete failure” to target help with energy bills at those most in need. It says:

blocks.text: double quotation markThe poorest half of households will gain £158 on average from cost of living support this year and next, just £14 more than the £144 received by the richest half – highlighting a complete failure to target help at those who need it most.

items: It says long-term public spending plans imply a return to austerity. It says:

blocks.text: double quotation markTight spending plans beyond 2028-29 imply departmental budgets will take more of the strain in the future. But if the 3% defence target is met and real health spending continues to grow at 2.6%, pencilled-in spending totals imply that funding for 13 ‘unprotected’ departments will fall to just 4.7% of GDP by 2031-32, close to the post-austerity historic low.

items: It says people will get poorer between now and the end of the parliament. It says:

blocks.text: double quotation markMedian real annual disposable incomes for working age households are set to grow by a paltry £600 over the course of the parliament. Worse still, those gains are already behind us. Between now (2026-27) and the end of the parliament (2028-29), typical incomes are forecast to fall in total by £1,050 (3 per cent).

This is one reason why so many people continue to think Andy Burnham will call an election next spring (before the electorate feels the full misery of getting poorer) – despite Burnham yesterday saying he would not hold one within the next 12 months.
Here is the agenda for the day.
9am: Jonathan Haskel, chair of the Office for Budget Responsibility, and Ruth Curtice, head of the Resolution Foundation, speak at an event where the RF is presenting its budget analysis.
9.30am: Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, takes questions in the Commons.
10.30am: Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, presents the IFS’s budget analysis.
11.30am: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.
After 11.30am: MPs resume the budget debate in the Commons.
Lunchtime: Andy Burnham is on a visit to a Rolls-Royce factory in the Midlands where he is speaking to the media.

articles.title: One Nation accuses PM of trying to ‘exert undue political influence’ by offering David Farley an extra staffer
articles.summary:
Pauline Hanson says Anthony Albanese made ‘unsolicited’ offer of adviser with $200,000 salary to one of her MPs

  • Get our

blocks.text: The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, offered the One Nation MP David Farley an additional staff member in what the party has called an “unsolicited” move, made in an attempt to win over the new politician using taxpayer funds.

In a statement posted on social media, Pauline Hanson claimed the move, which would cost taxpayers as much as $200,000 in additional salary, was an attempt to “exert undue political influence” over politicians.
She said the offer was received outside an existing request by One Nation for additional staffers.
“David did not request this allocation of staff. No reason was provided by the prime minister for the provision of this staff,” Hanson said.
The pair had also met privately over the past few weeks in meetings initiated by the prime minister, the statement added.

A letter authorising the MP for the New South Wales electorate of Farrer to hire another staff member was hand-delivered to Farley’s Parliament House office in Canberra on Monday by a member of the prime minister’s team, the Sydney Morning Herald reported.
Hanson said she was concerned Albanese was “seeking to use taxpayer funds to exert undue political influence over politicians”.
“We have decided to expose these grubby dealings because the public deserves to know what the Albanese Labor government is doing behind closed doors,” she said.
“For months, One Nation has been fighting for fair, transparent and objective allocation of staffing for parliamentarians. The prime minister has refused to respond to these calls.”
Farley, who rejected the “unsolicited” offer for an additional staffer, did not definitively rule out joining Labor.

“The attributes that I was looking for in a political party to represent Farrer is that I need political courage, I need political tenacity, and I made my decision to join One Nation,” he told News24 on Thursday.
“I know that I’ve still got that courage and tenacity in behind me. I have got a very, very clear and defined mandate.”
after newsletter promotion
Albanese was asked about staffing allocations on Thursday morning, including calls by the former Labor senator Fatima Payman for more funding.
He said Payman, who sits as an independent, had one more staff member than before she quit Labor to move to the crossbench.
Albanese did not answer questions about whether it was appropriate for the prime minister to be in charge of taxpayer-funded staffing allocations for MPs across parliament.
Hanson stood alongside independents Dai Le and Payman last month to demand consistent staffing resources.
“The prime minister should not personally control the resources available to his political opponents,” the One Nation leader said.
“While this power has always been open to abuse, it has, in our view, been weaponised to an unprecedented extent under this Labor government and this prime minister.”

articles.title: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
articles.summary: The acquisition of the warplanes comes amid ongoing fighting in northern Tigray region that started last month.

blocks.text: Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, as fighting intensified in the northern Tigray region neighbouring Eritrea.
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is attending the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, described the acquisition as a "milestone" that would boost Ethiopia's defence capacity.

He said Ethiopia and Russia agreed on the deal several years ago and the warplanes had come ahead of schedule. He also said that Ethiopia had plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow.
The Ethiopian leader said the military hardware was essential to protect the country from external threats.

Abiy, who described Russian President Vladimir Putin, "as a close friend of Ethiopia", said Ethiopia had now become the first country in sub‑Saharan Africa to own this kind of "advanced combat technology."
"If we fail to build this capability, surviving as a country in our region will become difficult. Countries with sufficient preparation are not easily defied," he said.
Russia and Ethiopia have signed several military agreements in recent years, including a deal in 2021 to train and improve technology for the military.
Abiy explained that Ethiopia signed an agreement with Russia several years ago to procure the Su‑35 jets and S‑400 systems, citing global air force trends and security threats facing the country.
The Su‑35, he noted, is equipped for both air‑to‑air and air‑to‑ground combat, with the ability to detect and neutralize incoming cruise missiles at distances of up to 200 kilometers.

Military intelligence analyst Qalaab Segatu told BBC Amharic that Ethiopia's acquisition of additional warplanes was a key indication that "it was preparing for possible wars with other countries, not just internal conflicts".
According to him, the jets are highly maneuverable and capable of covering large areas, with radars capable of ensuring air superiority and long-range scanning.

When combined, the fighter jets and air defence systems "create a significant capability to protect and defend major cities and critical infrastructure such as the Renaissance Dam, providing key strategic air superiority," Qalaab said.
Abiy said besides the advanced capabilities of the aircraft from Russia, the use of drones was equally important in strengthening deterrence.
Ethiopia has extensively used military drones, including those sourced from Turkey and China, in recent conflicts.
"We need to build capacity not only with drones, but also with the fourth generation capabilities of the Su 30 and Su 35 [aircraft]," Abiy said.

The latest acquisition of military hardware from Russia comes after the current conflict in northern Tigray started last month between the government and the party that controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF).
Both blame each other for violating a 2022 deal that ended a civil war.
Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the TPLF, which it denies.
Tensions between the two countries have also persisted as Abiy terms Ethiopia's lack of direct sea access an "existential question", which Eritrea views as a direct threat to its sovereignty.
Eritrea gained independence in 1993 after a decades-long war with Ethiopia, with the latter losing access to the sea.

articles.title: PNP reiterates call for Bato dela Rosa's surrender as deadline nears
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Thursday reiterated its appeal for Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa to surrender as the deadline set by the Department of the Interior and Local Government…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 4:21pm

The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Thursday reiterated its appeal for Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa to surrender as the deadline set by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) nears.
“Again, the same appeal that we are giving to him and his family. Let's end this with dignity on your part,” PNP spokesperson Police Colonel Allen Rae Co said during a press briefing.
Co said authorities want to avoid any violent encounters, injuries, or deaths during the ongoing manhunt for the senator.

“Let's avoid any untoward incidents, any potential dangerous encounters, or any harm that may come to anybody. We would like to avoid any injuries, any violent encounters, and of course, pinakamasama na po is mayroon pong masawi dito sa (worst, fatalities in the) operation,” he said.
The one-week deadline given by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) for Dela Rosa to surrender expires on Friday.
Co declined to disclose specific details of its manhunt operations as this could compromise the efforts of police personnel and put them in danger.
He noted that authorities are not expecting wanted individuals to remain in one place. For him, intensified operations and the announcement of a reward could restrict Dela Rosa's movements.
The government has offered a P50-million reward for information that could lead to the senator's location and arrest.

Co clarified that the reward is intended for individuals who can provide tips or information to authorities, and not for civilians to personally arrest the senator or take the law into their own hands.
Dela Rosa, a former PNP chief, is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in connection with the crimes against humanity case arising from former President Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs.
The senator is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes.
The DILG earlier claimed that Dela Rosa was hiding in Mindanao under the protection of an “armed and powerful group,” but did not identify the group. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Hello Kitty company cuts ties with Japanese spy show after China outcry
articles.summary:
Sanrio ends association with TV drama Vivant after China says portrayal of ruthless Chinese agents is ‘deliberate smear’

The company behind the successful

blocks.text: The company behind the successful Hello Kitty franchise has apologised and ended its commercial tie-up with a Japanese TV drama after Chinese state media and netizens condemned the show’s “deliberate smears” against China.

Sanrio, a Japanese firm whose characters are popular around the world, said in a post on the Chinese social media site Weibo that it had decided to end its association with the TV drama Vivant after concluding that it “contained elements inconsistent with Sanrio’s core values”.
In the second season of the popular spy thriller, produced by the Japanese TBS network, Masato Sakai plays a salaryman who is drawn into a web of international crime and espionage.

The backlash began this week when Chinese state media blasted the portrayal of Chinese agents using “ruthless violence” to torture members of a secret unit of Japan’s self-defence forces, calling it a “deliberate smear” against Beijing.
Chinese media said that some of the torture methods were similar to those Japanese troops used against Chinese civilians during the second world war.

The state-run tabloid Global Times said the acts shown in the episode “bear striking similarities to the torture inflicted on Chinese nationals by invading Japanese troops” during the war, adding that the drama “distorts the truth by attributing these atrocities to modern Chinese characters”.
In the 4 October episode, a Chinese agent is seen cutting off the fingers of the Japanese intelligence officer and stabbing him in the abdomen.

Sanrio said in a statement: “Since its inception, Sanrio has consistently used its characters to convey values such as care and connection, and remains committed to its corporate philosophy of fostering harmony among all people.
“We take the feedback we have received regarding this incident very seriously. Moving forward, we will strengthen our review processes for all future collaborative projects.”
The drama’s first season, set in a fictional central Asian country, avoided controversy, but its latest season is being shown at a time of increasingly fractious relations between Beijing and Tokyo.

Japan’s conservative prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, set off a diplomatic row in November last year when she told MPs that a Chinese attack on Taiwan could trigger the deployment of her country’s self-defence forces if the conflict posed an existential threat to Japan.
Takaichi said earlier this month that she had recorded episodes of Vivant and hoped to watch them over the year-end and new year holidays.
China is a crucial overseas market for Sanrio, whose cast of characters includes My Melody and Cinnamoroll – both featured in Vivant-themed merchandise.
The Tokyo-based company racked up 781m yuan ($117m) in revenue from the Chinese market in the first half of this year, according to Chinese media, up more than 40% from the same period last year.

The backlash against Sanrio comes days after the French international footballer Kylian Mbappé was dropped by several Chinese brands after he jokingly referred to Mao Zedong as a “dictator”. The Real Madrid forward, who is nicknamed the “dictator” for his influence on the game, later apologised for his “ill-judged” remarks.
